scope: Independent immutable-build, isolated HTTP/service, and source-level app review; no actual browser controls or DOM observations

passedEvidence.covers: Source/build/spec pins, private copies, sanitized public manifest, six canonical checkpoints and six scheduled events
Sequential route allowlist, static bytes, API validation and lifecycle, capacity, clock-controlled expiry, redacted logs

blockingFindings.title: Overlapping request IDs are not locked before asynchronous logging
blockingFindings.observed: Identical concurrent start returned 201/201 with two distinct attempts; identical concurrent commit returned 201/409 attempt_locked rather than the same receipt; conflicting concurrent start reuse returned 201/201 for T01 and T02. The same failure was exercised directly and over an isolated HTTP server.
blockingFindings.minimalFix: Reserve an in-flight request identity and canonical payload before the first await. Identical overlapping retries join the original result; conflicting reuse rejects without another mutation. Preserve the immutable first response and event identity.

blockingFindings.title: Late ledger export can repopulate answer-bearing text after canonical restoration
blockingFindings.observed: The ledger export awaits the server without marking a pending action or capturing mode, epoch, session and case. Reopen saved remains enabled and clears export text, but the earlier export response then writes its revealed target/explanation into export-output unconditionally on the canonical page.
blockingFindings.minimalFix: Bind the export response to its initiating document epoch/session/mode and discard it after navigation, or keep navigation disabled for the entire export operation; canonical restoration must leave export text empty.

blockingFindings.title: Actual API acknowledgement and rejection UI events are labeled scripted demonstration
blockingFindings.observed: The event logger maps every origin other than user-control to scripted_demonstration. The actual attempt/commit/reveal/session API acknowledgements and rejections call it with origin api, so the exported UI ledger states false actor/provenance.
blockingFindings.minimalFix: Map api events to a distinct software API actor/provenance, while retaining scripted_demonstration only for replay and automatic events.

blockingFindings.title: Play and boundary pause can emit nonchaining before/after fingerprints
blockingFindings.observed: Play captures before before an implicit restore from local review: restore emits local-to-paused-canonical, then tour-play again claims the old local before. Pause captures before before advanceClock; when that call emits a scheduled case-select, tour-pause repeats a pre-boundary before. In both reachable paths, adjacent event fingerprints differ at their join.
blockingFindings.minimalFix: For each event, capture before immediately after any preceding state-changing operation, or emit the control transition in the actual order so each event's before equals the preceding event's after.

boundedNonblockingNotes: The synchronous event export has no late server response, and pending start/commit/reveal guard their epoch, case and attempt before applying acknowledgements.

A failed /api/session creation currently clears pending/unknown without an idempotency key. Because the frozen /api/session schema has no requestId and session creation is a separate pre-attempt operation, this is recorded as a session-issuance ambiguity rather than an additional candidate blocker; it must not be described as a proven idempotent session retry.

Close on navigation is fire-and-forget; an unacknowledged close can leave a server attempt open until a later start or expiry. Local history is not falsely marked abandoned from that path; the host should inspect actual ledgers.
credentialsAndReceipts: Redacted from the summarized failure reproduction; no credential or receipt values are quoted in this report.
